offending.filing: Plaintiff's December 2024 motion for a protective order
offending.court_quote: Counsel first cited fabricated authority in plaintiff's December 2024 motion for a protective order, relying on “People v. O'Keefe, 2019 WL 6907273,” regarding the exclusion of cumulative expert testimony. Defendant identified the fabricated citation in response.

offending.filing: Plaintiff's February 2025 motion for a new trial or evidentiary hearing
offending.court_quote: In plaintiff's February 2025 motion seeking a new trial or evidentiary hearing based on juror misconduct, counsel cited two nonexistent criminal cases, “People v. Stubblefield, 197 Mich. App. 365 (1992),” and “People v. Royster, 291 Mich. App. 508 (2011).”

offending.filing: Plaintiff's February 2025 motion for a new trial or evidentiary hearing
offending.court_quote: In plaintiff's February 2025 motion seeking a new trial or evidentiary hearing based on juror misconduct, counsel cited two nonexistent criminal cases, “People v. Stubblefield, 197 Mich. App. 365 (1992),” and “People v. Royster, 291 Mich. App. 508 (2011).”

offending.filing: Plaintiff's brief on appeal, Michigan Court of Appeals No. 374773
offending.court_quote: In plaintiff's brief in this Court, counsel cited “Meyer v. Walker, 241 Mich. App. 295 (2000),” a case that does not exist, for propositions concerning presumed prejudice and the standard of review.
offending.what_actually_exists: Nothing under this name; counsel later conceded in a Notice of Correction that “Meyer is not a real case.”

offending.quoted_text: trial court's handling of juror misconduct allegations is reviewed for an abuse of discretion
offending.court_quote: Counsel also repeatedly cited real authorities for propositions they do not support. For example, counsel cited People v Budzyn, 456 Mich 77; 566 NW2d 229 (1997), for the proposition that a “trial court's handling of juror misconduct allegations is reviewed for an abuse of discretion,” but Budzyn states no such standard.
offending.what_actually_exists: People v Budzyn, 456 Mich 77 (1997) is a real Michigan Supreme Court decision but states no such standard of review.

offending.quoted_text: trial court's management of trial procedures, including exhibit availability and deliberation duration
offending.court_quote: Counsel similarly cited People v Miller, 482 Mich 540; 759 NW2d 850 (2008), for the proposition that a “trial court's management of trial procedures, including exhibit availability and deliberation duration” is reviewed for an abuse of discretion, but Miller addressed neither issue. In short, most of the citations in plaintiff's initial brief on appeal do not support the propositions for which they are offered.
offending.what_actually_exists: People v Miller, 482 Mich 540 (2008) is real but addressed neither exhibit availability nor deliberation duration.

offending.filing: Plaintiff's counsel's "Notice of Correction" on appeal
offending.court_quote: But the Notice of Correction did not cure the problem. Counsel purported to substitute valid authorities for the fabricated and unsupported ones, but those substitute authorities still did not support the propositions for which counsel offered them. Most notably, counsel attributed to Miller, 482 Mich at 548-552, quotations concerning “extraneous prejudicial information” and “outside influence.” Those phrases do not appear in Miller. They appear instead in MRE 606(b)(2), which Miller does not discuss.
offending.what_actually_exists: The quoted phrases appear in Michigan Rule of Evidence 606(b)(2), not in People v Miller; Miller does not discuss that rule.
